text:
Raj: hey team — quick onboarding Qs from my first week (UK-based). 1) my commuter card top-up link says 'not eligible' even though i selected Commuter in benefits. 2) payroll shows me as 'resident' for tax withholding but i'm on a Tier 2 visa and submitted a tax treaty form (I think form 8233?). who do i ping to correct withholding?
People Ops: welcome, Raj! for commuter eligibility we sync with the benefits vendor after your payroll enrollment processes. sometimes the commuter toggle doesn't stick if your bank details haven't been verified. did you complete the 'bank verification' step under Profile > Payments?
Raj: yep did that (bank verified yesterday). commuter link still shows 'not eligible'. i attached a screenshot. also i uploaded a pdf called "Tax_Treaty_Raj.pdf" under Payroll > Tax Docs last week.
Sam (Payroll): hi @Raj — thanks. nonresident tax treaty docs often require a specific code in our payroll system. can you confirm the filename and date of upload? i'll check the intake queue. Also, Form 8233 is for claiming exemption on compensation for certain nonresident aliens; are you getting U.S. payroll or UK payroll?
Raj: i'm on US payroll (relocated remotely to UK temporarily) — i uploaded Tax_Treaty_Raj.pdf on 1923390000.
Benefits Vendor Bot: subscription sync job ran: commuter_status=not eligible for employee=RWI-4152 reason=policy_mismatch. Please open a vendor support ticket with category=commuter-eligibility.
People Ops: thanks bot. @Sam i'll need a short confirmation that the payroll tax doc was processed before i file the vendor ticket (they require payroll confirmation to change commuter eligibility for cross-border employees).
Sam (Payroll): checking now. Raj, i see an uploaded file but it failed automated validation — missing signature page. can you re-upload the signed 8233 (page 3) or an employer certification? Quick tip: use mobile capture in the portal for best results. once i mark it as "validated" we'll re-run the commuter eligibility sync.
Raj: ah — i thought the signature was on page 1. re-uploading signed page 3 now. attached as 1923456805-8233-sig.jpg
Raj: also quick unrelated Q — holiday accrual: i start mid-month. do i get prorated UK bank holidays for this calendar month or full accrual from next month?
People Ops: UK statutory holidays are prorated from your start date for the first year. Contract also lists 20 days PTO pro-rated. We calculate accrual on a monthly basis and the payroll system applies pro-rate on the next pay run. You should see the pro-rated balance in Self-Service > Leave within 1 pay cycle.
Sam (Payroll): uploaded new file and validated tax doc for RWI-4152 at 1923456812. Marked employee as "nonresident treaty claimed" in payroll. Will dispatch an update to benefits sync.
Benefits Vendor Bot: vendor ticket created: ticket=BV-72819; action=review commuter eligibility after payroll confirmation. ETA 48h.
Finance: FYI — for cross-border reimbursements (relocation stipend), our policy says reimbursements may be treated differently for tax purposes; finance will need the country of residence on the expense. Ping finance@redwood.com when you submit the relocation claim.
Raj: amazing, thanks everyone. will re-upload and submit relocation claim with country set to UK. tagging resolved for now — i'll reopen if the commuter card still shows not eligible after 48h. :pray:
